extra.official_description: Alibaba's text-to-video model for cinematic clips and spoken scenes, with native sound and lip sync. It makes a 3 to 15 second clip at 720P or 1080P, including ultrawide and tall frames, with clearer motion than HappyHorse 1.0.
Alibaba's image-to-video model for animating a still into a spoken or cinematic scene, with native sound. It makes a 3 to 15 second clip at 720P or 1080P.
Alibaba's reference-to-video model for a scene that keeps several characters consistent, with native sound. It uses 1 to 9 reference images in a 3 to 15 second clip at 720P or 1080P.
Alibaba's text-to-video model for cinematic clips with native sound and lip sync. It makes a 3 to 15 second clip at 720P or 1080P, including ultrawide and tall frames.
Alibaba's image-to-video model for animating a still with native sound. It makes a 3 to 15 second clip at 720P or 1080P.
Alibaba's reference-to-video model for a scene built from several character images, with native sound. It uses 1 to 9 reference images in a 3 to 15 second clip at 720P or 1080P.
Alibaba's video editor for restyling a clip or changing its scene while keeping the source motion. It can use up to five reference images and returns a 720P or 1080P result.
Alibaba's text-to-image model for newspapers, storyboards, menus, and other dense layouts. It renders small multilingual text and photographic detail, and can return up to six images at up to 2K.
Alibaba's image editor for precise changes to dense layouts and small text. It uses 1 to 3 reference images and can return up to six results at up to 2K.
Alibaba's faster text-to-image model for dense layouts, readable text, and photographic stills. It can return up to six images at up to 2K, with a quicker turnaround than Qwen Image 3.0 Pro.
Alibaba's faster image editor for instruction changes across a few references. It uses 1 to 3 images and can return up to six results at up to 2K.
Alibaba's text-to-video model for longer scenes with optional sound. It makes a 2 to 30 second clip at 480P, 720P, or 1080P, in widescreen, square, or vertical frames.
Alibaba's image-to-video model for animating a start frame, bridging two frames, or following up to 10 reference images, with optional sound. It makes a 2 to 30 second clip at 480P, 720P, or 1080P.
Alibaba's video model for rebuilding a clip from reference video, images, and audio. It uses 1 to 5 videos in a 2 to 30 second result at 480P, 720P, or 1080P.
Alibaba's text-to-video model for multi-shot scenes with synchronized sound. It makes a 2 to 15 second clip at 720P or 1080P, and can follow a supplied audio track.
Alibaba's image-to-video model for animating a start frame, bridging two frames, or continuing a clip, with synchronized sound. It makes a 2 to 15 second clip at 720P or 1080P.
Alibaba's reference-to-video model for a clip guided by images or short videos, with synchronized sound. It makes a 720P or 1080P result in widescreen, square, or vertical frames.
Alibaba's text-to-image model for brand visuals, readable text, and a connected set of images. It renders at 1K, 2K, or 4K, and can return up to 12 related frames.
Alibaba's image editor for multi-reference changes and a connected set of results. It uses 1 to 9 images and returns results at up to 2K, including a set of up to 12 related frames.
Alibaba's faster text-to-image model for brand visuals and a connected set of images. It renders at 1K or 2K and can return up to 12 related frames.
Alibaba's faster image editor for multi-reference changes and a connected set of results. It uses 1 to 9 images and returns results at up to 2K.
Alibaba's fast text-to-image model for photorealistic portraits, product shots, and quick drafts.
Alibaba's high-quality text-to-speech model for narration, audiobooks, and brand voiceovers. It speaks with system voices in Chinese or English, and can read styled delivery and formulas.
Alibaba's low-latency text-to-speech model for voice assistants, prompts, and short announcements. It speaks with a wider set of system voices than CosyVoice v3 Plus, including Chinese dialects.
Alibaba's voice-design model for one-off speech in a voice described in words. It designs the voice and speaks the text in the same request, in Chinese or English.
Alibaba's voice-clone model for speaking new text in the voice of a short reference clip. It covers Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, and several other languages.
Alibaba's high-quality text-to-speech model for premium narration and brand voiceovers. It speaks in Chinese or English, and can follow a style instruction.
Alibaba's low-latency text-to-speech model for voice assistants and short prompts. It speaks in Chinese or English, with a quicker first response than Qwen Audio 3.0 TTS Plus.
Alibaba's speech-to-text model for recorded meetings, calls, and captions. It can bias recognition with a custom vocabulary, label speakers, and take a language hint.
ByteDance's fast text-to-video model for short stories, social clips, and rapid creative iteration, with native sound. It generates 4 to 30 second videos at 480p or 720p.

ByteDance's fast image-to-video model for animating a starting frame or connecting a first and last frame, with native sound. It generates 4 to 30 second clips at 480p or 720p while preserving the starting image's aspect ratio.

ByteDance's fast reference-image video model for character-led scenes, product shots, and visual storytelling, with optional reference audio and native sound. It combines up to 10 reference images in a 4 to 30 second clip at 480p or 720p.

ByteDance's fast video model for editing, extending, or creating a new clip from reference video, with native sound. It accepts up to five videos with optional image and audio references and produces 480p or 720p output.
ByteDance's text-to-video model for longer stories told in one clip, with native sound. It makes a 4 to 30 second clip at 480p, 720p, or 1080p, in widescreen, square, or vertical frames.
ByteDance's image-to-video model for animating a starting frame, with an optional end frame and reference audio. It makes a 4 to 30 second clip at 480p, 720p, or 1080p, with native sound.

ByteDance's reference-to-video model for a scene built from many images, with optional reference audio and native sound. It uses 1 to 30 reference images in a 4 to 30 second clip at 480p, 720p, or 1080p.

ByteDance's video model for editing, extending, or rebuilding a clip from reference video, with native sound. It uses up to 10 videos, plus optional images and audio, and can make a 4 to 30 second result at up to 1080p.
ByteDance's text-to-video model for cinematic clips with native sound, including a 4K master. It makes a 4 to 15 second clip at 480p, 720p, 1080p, or 4K.

ByteDance's image-to-video model for animating a start frame, bridging two frames, or following up to nine reference images, with native sound. It makes a 4 to 15 second clip at 480p, 720p, 1080p, or 4K.
ByteDance's video editor for restyling or rebuilding a clip from reference video, images, and audio, with native sound. It uses 1 to 3 videos in a 4 to 15 second result at up to 4K.
ByteDance's fast text-to-video model for drafts and quick iterations with native sound. It makes a 4 to 15 second clip at 480p or 720p.
ByteDance's fast image-to-video model for animating a start frame, bridging two frames, or following up to nine reference images. It makes a 4 to 15 second clip at 480p or 720p, with native sound.
ByteDance's fast video editor for restyling a clip from reference video, images, and audio. It uses 1 to 3 videos in a 4 to 15 second result at 480p or 720p, with native sound.
ByteDance's lightweight text-to-video model for high-volume drafts and social clips with native sound. It makes a 4 to 15 second clip at 480p or 720p.
ByteDance's lightweight image-to-video model for high-volume drafts from a start frame, two frames, or up to nine reference images. It makes a 4 to 15 second clip at 480p or 720p, with native sound.
ByteDance's lightweight video editor for high-volume restyles from reference video, images, and audio. It uses 1 to 3 videos in a 4 to 15 second result at 480p or 720p, with native sound.

ByteDance's image editing model for consistent visual revisions, reference-guided compositions, and reusable design layers. It blends multiple references, produces transparent assets, and separates a single image into layers with rich-text recognition for regular text.

ByteDance's flagship text-to-image model for professional design, photorealistic shots, and brand visuals. It returns one finished image at up to 2K, with precise placement, readable text, and consistent quality.
ByteDance's image editor for precise changes to one picture, including layout, color, and a marked region. It returns one result at up to 2K.
ByteDance's reasoning text-to-image model for infographics, text-heavy designs, and images that draw on current knowledge. It renders at 2K or 3K and can return a set of related images.
ByteDance's reasoning image editor for instruction-based changes across several references. It uses 1 to 14 images and can return a set of related results at 2K or 3K.

Google's fast text-to-image model for high-volume production, readable posters and diagrams, and rapid iteration. It keeps Flash-level speed at 1K, 2K, and 4K, with stronger visual quality, text rendering, and real-world knowledge than Nano Banana 2.

Google's fast image editor for posters, product shots, and scenes that have to stay consistent. It edits up to 14 reference images, or a video together with images, at 1K, 2K, or 4K, with stronger character consistency and text rendering than Nano Banana 2.
Google's fast text-to-image model for high-volume drafts, stylized graphics, and readable posters. It renders at 512, 1K, 2K, or 4K, including extra-wide and extra-tall frames.
Google's fast image editor for style changes, quick revisions, and frames taken from a video. It uses up to 14 reference images and returns a result at 512, 1K, 2K, or 4K.
Google's fastest text-to-image model for high-volume drafts, thumbnails, and stylized stills. It returns a 1K image, including vertical 9:16 and ultrawide 21:9 frames.
Google's fast image editor for high-volume style changes and quick revisions. It edits up to 14 images, or a video together with images, and returns a 1K result.
Google's premium text-to-image model for professional assets, brand layouts, and complex instructions. It renders at 1K, 2K, or 4K, with precise text and consistent subjects.
Google's premium image editor for detailed creative changes, background replacements, and style work. It uses up to 14 reference images and returns a result at 1K, 2K, or 4K.
Google's fast text-to-image model for quick sketches, stylized ideas, and early visual drafts, in square, portrait, or widescreen frames.
Google's fast image editor for straightforward instruction edits. It uses 1 to 3 images together as the reference for the change.
Google's cinematic text-to-video model for short films, ads, and scenes with native sound. It makes a 4, 6, or 8 second clip in widescreen or vertical frames, and can render 1080p or 4K.

Google's cinematic image-to-video model for animating a still, bridging two frames, or following up to three reference images, with native sound. It makes a 4, 6, or 8 second clip in widescreen or vertical frames, and can render 1080p or 4K.
Google's fast text-to-video model for drafts, social clips, and high-volume ads with native sound. It makes a 4, 6, or 8 second clip in widescreen or vertical frames, and can render 1080p or 4K.

Google's fast image-to-video model for animating a still, bridging two frames, or matching up to three reference images, with native sound. It makes a 4, 6, or 8 second clip in widescreen or vertical frames, and can render 1080p or 4K.
Google's efficient text-to-video model for high-volume social clips and ads with native sound. It makes a 4, 6, or 8 second clip at 720p or 1080p, in widescreen or vertical frames.
Google's image-to-video model for animating a still or bridging a start and end frame, with native sound. It makes a 4, 6, or 8 second clip at 720p or 1080p, in widescreen or vertical frames.

Google's video generation model for turning text into short scenes with synchronized sound. It suits product concepts, narrative clips, and storyboard exploration across landscape and portrait formats.

Image-to-video generation for animating product imagery, characters, and visual concepts. A starting image anchors the opening frame, and an optional ending image guides the transition while the model generates synchronized audio.

Reference-guided video generation for carrying visual appearance and motion ideas into new scenes. It combines image and video references with a text prompt for character concepts, product scenes, and mixed-reference storyboards.

Prompt-driven video editing for restyling scenes, changing lighting, and revising visual details in existing footage. Optional image references guide the transformation while the output follows the source clip's duration and aspect ratio.

Video continuation for extending an action, continuing a camera move, or completing a short scene. It uses the source ending and optional image references to generate a new segment and returns it joined to the retained source footage.

Google's text-to-video model for short social and concept clips with synchronized speech, music, and sound effects. It makes a 3 to 10 second clip at 360p, 720p, 1080p, or 4K, in widescreen or vertical frames.
Google's image-to-video model for bringing a still to life with synchronized sound. It uses one starting frame in a 3 to 10 second clip at 360p, 720p, 1080p, or 4K.

Google's video editor for changing the scene, mood, style, or lighting of a short clip, with synchronized sound. It keeps the source length and frame shape, and can render the result at 360p, 720p, 1080p, or 4K.

Google's studio text-to-speech model for audiobooks, long narration, and expressive two-speaker scenes. It covers 130 languages and follows turn-by-turn delivery, including a designed or library voice.

Google's fast text-to-speech model for voice agents, read-aloud, and high-volume narration. It covers 101 languages, with single-speaker speech or a two-speaker scene, at lower latency than Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS.

Google's speech-to-text model for meetings, captions, and call recordings. It recognizes 85 or more languages in a public audio file of up to 15 minutes, and can label up to 8 speakers, add word timestamps, or clean up the wording.
Google's low-latency text-to-speech model for voiceovers, presenters, and two-person dialogue. It speaks with one of 30 preset voices and can follow a style direction for pace and emotion.

Kling's reasoning text-to-video model for complex physical motion and scenes that have to follow the prompt closely. It makes a 3 to 10 second clip at 720p or 1080p, in widescreen, square, or vertical frames.
Kling's reasoning image-to-video model for complex motion grounded in reference frames. It uses 1 to 7 reference images in a 3 to 10 second clip at 720p or 1080p.
Kling's reasoning video model for editing a clip from a reference video while keeping the source motion. It uses one reference video and up to four images in a 3 to 10 second clip at 720p or 1080p.

Kling's reasoning image model for complex layouts and blends of reference subjects. It uses up to 10 reference images and returns up to 9 results at 1K or 2K, including vertical 9:16 and ultrawide 21:9 frames.

Kling's storyboard text-to-video model for multi-beat scenes and consistent characters, with optional native sound and automatic shot changes. It makes a 3 to 15 second clip at 720p, 1080p, or 4K, in widescreen, square, or vertical frames.

Kling's reference-to-video model for a scene that keeps subjects and style consistent, with optional native sound and automatic shot changes. It uses 1 to 7 reference images in a 3 to 15 second clip at 720p, 1080p, or 4K.

Kling's video-to-video model for restyling or changing a clip from a reference video, with optional stills and sound. It uses one reference video and up to four images in a 3 to 15 second clip at 720p, 1080p, or 4K.
Kling's fast text-to-video model for short-form drafts and high-volume clips. It makes a 3 to 15 second clip at 720p or 1080p, in widescreen, square, or vertical frames.
Kling's fast image-to-video model for turning one still into a short clip. It makes a 3 to 15 second video at 720p or 1080p.

Kling's text-to-video model for cinematic scenes and longer shots, with optional native sound and automatic shot changes. It makes a 3 to 15 second clip at 720p, 1080p, or 4K, in widescreen, square, or vertical frames.
Kling's image-to-video model for animating a still into a longer scene, with an optional end frame, native sound, and automatic shot changes. It makes a 3 to 15 second clip at 720p, 1080p, or 4K.
Kling's text-to-image model for concept art and photorealistic stills. It returns up to 9 images at 1K or 2K, including vertical 9:16 and ultrawide 21:9 frames.
Kling's effects model for turning one or two photos into a short themed clip, such as a dance or a bullet-time shot. It applies a preset effect in a 5 or 10 second video.
Kling's talking-avatar model for presenters and portrait performances. It lip-syncs one portrait to an audio track or a generated voice, with expression and camera direction in the prompt.
Kling's image expansion model for extending a cropped photo or widening its frame while the original picture stays. It can grow any side by up to twice that edge and return up to 9 variations.
Text-to-video generation for advertising concepts, storyboards, and short narrative scenes. It combines prompt-directed composition and widescreen framing to turn scene ideas into finished clips.
Image-to-video generation for animating product shots, characters, and illustrated scenes. First, middle, and final keyframes guide the visual progression for planned motion and scene transitions.

Reference-guided video editing for removing objects, restyling scenes, and revising existing footage. Image, video, and subject references help guide changes while keeping the surrounding scene and recognizable subjects consistent.
Fast text-to-video generation for product previews, advertising drafts, and short social clips. It combines prompt-directed scenes and flexible framing for frequent creative iteration.
Single-image animation for product showcases, character motion, and social video. It turns a starting image into a short clip, using the reference to guide the opening composition.

Video editing in the Flash series for scene restyling, object changes, and reference-guided revisions. It combines source footage with image, video, or subject references to shape the resulting scene.

Microsoft's text-to-image model for marketing visuals, product shots, portraits, and posters that need readable text. It improves text rendering, portraits, and photorealistic commercial images over MAI Image 2.5, with each side from 768 to 1365 pixels.
Microsoft's image-editing model for targeted object changes, layout updates, text cleanup, and photorealistic retouching on one image. It keeps the rest of the composition in place.

Microsoft's faster text-to-image model for high-volume drafts, interactive tools, and production pipelines, with lower latency than MAI Image 2.6. It keeps the same text rendering and portrait range, with each side from 768 to 1365 pixels.

Microsoft's faster image-editing model for high-volume retouching, object changes, and text cleanup on one image, with lower latency than MAI Image 2.6 Edit. It keeps the rest of the composition in place.

Microsoft's speech-to-text model for meeting notes, captions, and call transcripts across 43 languages. It transcribes a public WAV, MP3, or FLAC file of up to 300 MB, with an optional language hint and a phrase list for names.

MiniMax's fast text-to-video model for prompt-only drafts and short scenes, with picture and sound together. It makes a 5 to 15 second clip at 480p or 768p, including vertical 9:16 and ultrawide 21:9 frames.

MiniMax's fast reference-to-video model for drafts that keep a subject or style consistent, with picture and sound together. It uses 1 to 9 reference images and up to three audio clips, in a 5 to 15 second clip at 480p or 768p.
MiniMax's fast first-and-last-frame model for drafts that open on a still, land on an end frame, or bridge both, with picture and sound together. It makes a 5 to 15 second clip at 480p or 768p.

MiniMax's fast video-to-video model for drafts guided by reference motion, with optional stills and audio, and picture and sound together. It uses 1 to 3 reference videos in a 5 to 15 second clip at 480p or 768p.

MiniMax's text-to-video model for storyboards, character shorts, and cinematic b-roll from a prompt, with picture and sound together. It makes a 4 to 15 second clip at 768p or 2K, including vertical 9:16 and ultrawide 21:9 frames.

MiniMax's reference-to-video model for a new scene that keeps characters, products, or a style consistent, with picture and sound together. It uses 1 to 9 reference images and up to three audio clips, in a 4 to 15 second clip at 768p or 2K.
MiniMax's first-and-last-frame model for opening on a still, landing on an end frame, or bridging both, with picture and sound together. It makes a 4 to 15 second clip at 768p or 2K.

MiniMax's video-to-video model for a new clip guided by reference motion, with optional stills and audio, and picture and sound together. It uses 1 to 3 reference videos in a 4 to 15 second clip at 768p or 2K.
MiniMax's text-to-video model for character performance, stylized looks, and physical action from a prompt. It makes a 6 or 10 second clip at 768p, and a 6 second clip at 1080p.

MiniMax's image-to-video model for animating a portrait or illustrated still with facial detail and physical motion. The image stays the opening frame, in a 6 or 10 second clip at 768p, or a 6 second clip at 1080p.
MiniMax's faster image-to-video model for rapid drafts and batch clips from one still. The image stays the opening frame, in a 6 or 10 second clip at 768p, or a 6 second clip at 1080p.
MiniMax's text-to-video model for product shots, sports, and wide scenes that need physical motion and close prompt following. It makes a 6 or 10 second clip at 768p, and a 6 second clip at 1080p.
MiniMax's image-to-video model for animating a product photo or a wide scene with physical motion. It makes a 6 or 10 second clip at 512p or 768p, and a 6 second clip at 1080p.
MiniMax's first-and-last-frame model for morphs and storyboard transitions that land on a chosen end image. It bridges the frames in a 6 or 10 second clip at 768p, or a 6 second clip at 1080p.

MiniMax's high-quality text-to-speech model for narration, brand voices, and dialogue with breaths, laughs, and other spoken cues. It covers 40 languages, with emotion, a mix of up to four voices, and optional subtitles.

MiniMax's faster text-to-speech model for assistants and high-volume voiceover, with natural flow and the same spoken cues as Speech 2.8 HD. It covers 40 languages, with emotion, a mix of up to four voices, and optional subtitles.

MiniMax's voice-cloning model for narration and personal messages in a speaker's own voice, including breath and pace. It clones from a reference recording of 10 seconds to 5 minutes, then speaks new text with emotion and pitch control.

OpenAI's most capable text-to-image model for campaign creative, polished product imagery, and detailed illustrations. It renders at 1K, 2K, or 4K, including vertical 9:16 and ultrawide 21:9 frames, with transparent backgrounds and quality up to max.
OpenAI's most capable image-editing model for campaign changes, product retouching, and masked local edits. It works from 1 to 16 reference images at 1K, 2K, or 4K, including transparent backgrounds.

OpenAI's fast text-to-image model for social content, product shots, and high-volume drafts, with higher image quality and lower latency than GPT Image 2. It renders at 1K, 2K, or 4K, including vertical 9:16 and ultrawide 21:9 frames, with transparent backgrounds and quality up to max.

OpenAI's fast image-editing model for everyday retouching, product changes, and masked local edits. It works from 1 to 16 reference images at 1K, 2K, or 4K, including transparent backgrounds, with lower latency than GPT Image 2 Edit.

OpenAI's text-to-image model for detailed portraits, product shots, and cinematic frames at high resolution. It renders preset sizes up to 4K, including 3840x2160 and vertical 2160x3840, at low, medium, or high quality.
OpenAI's image-editing model for high-resolution retouching, style changes, and masked local edits. It works from 1 to 16 source images and can return sizes up to 4K, including 3840x2160.

OpenAI's speech-to-text model for meeting notes, podcasts, and captions from a public audio file of up to 25 MB. It can return plain text, subtitles, or word and segment timestamps, with an optional language hint.

PixVerse's cinematic text-to-video model for complex motion, visual effects, and film-style shots from a prompt, with optional synchronized sound. It makes a 1 to 15 second clip from 360p through 1080p, including vertical 9:16 and ultrawide 21:9 frames.

PixVerse's cinematic image-to-video model for animating one still with complex motion and visual effects, and optional synchronized sound. The image stays the opening frame, in a 1 to 15 second clip from 360p through 1080p.

PixVerse's cinematic first-and-last-frame model for effects-heavy transitions that have to land on a specific end image, with optional sound. It bridges the two images in a 1 to 15 second clip from 360p through 1080p.

PixVerse's cinematic reference-to-video model for effects-heavy scenes that keep characters and backgrounds consistent while the action moves, with optional sound. It uses 1 to 7 reference images in a 1 to 15 second clip from 360p through 1080p, including vertical 9:16 and ultrawide 21:9 frames.

PixVerse's text-to-video model for narrative clips, product shots, and social videos from a prompt, with optional sound and multi-clip cuts. It makes a 1 to 15 second clip from 360p through 1080p, including vertical 9:16 and ultrawide 21:9 frames.

PixVerse's image-to-video model for bringing one still to life as a product shot, illustration, or short scene, with optional sound and multi-clip cuts. The image stays the opening frame, in a 1 to 15 second clip from 360p through 1080p.

PixVerse's first-and-last-frame model for morphs, before-and-after shots, and transitions with a clear start and end, with optional sound. It bridges the two images in a 1 to 15 second clip from 360p through 1080p.

PixVerse's reference-to-video model for a new scene that keeps specific characters, products, or backgrounds recognizable, with optional sound. It uses 1 to 7 reference images in a 1 to 15 second clip from 360p through 1080p, including vertical 9:16 and ultrawide 21:9 frames.
PixVerse's video extension model for carrying a scene forward and adding an ending. It appends 1 to 15 seconds at 360p, 540p, 720p, or 1080p.
PixVerse's motion-control model for making a person or animal in a still follow the movement of a reference video, such as a dance or an action. It outputs the performance at 360p, 540p, or 720p.
PixVerse's video upscale model for sharpening an existing clip and raising its clarity before delivery. The picture, motion, and content stay the same.
PixVerse's video restyle model for giving existing footage a new look, such as felt, origami, ukiyo-e, clay, or a style described in words. The motion stays while the picture is re-rendered.

Vidu's image-to-video model for extending one still into a short clip with dialogue, sound effects, and camera movement. The image stays the opening frame, in a 3 to 16 second clip from 540p through 4K.

Vidu's reference-to-video model for a newly composed shot that keeps characters, style, and voices consistent across camera changes. It uses 1 to 15 reference images and up to three audio clips, in a 3 to 16 second clip from 540p through 4K, including 3:4 and 4:3 frames.

Vidu's cinematic text-to-video model for short films, ads, and concept scenes, with synchronized sound and automatic shot changes. It makes a 1 to 16 second clip at 540p, 720p, or 1080p, including vertical 9:16 and 3:4 frames.

Vidu's cinematic image-to-video model for concept art, commercials, and stills that need stable characters, complex motion, and synchronized sound. It animates one opening frame into a 1 to 16 second clip at 540p, 720p, or 1080p.

Vidu's cinematic first-and-last-frame model for commercial transitions and storyboard shots that need a clear path between two images. It bridges the start and end frames in a 1 to 16 second clip at 540p, 720p, or 1080p.

Vidu's fast image-to-video model for prototypes, product shots, and quick motion from a single still, with picture and sound together. It animates that frame into a 1 to 16 second clip at 720p or 1080p.

Vidu's fast text-to-video model for drafts, b-roll, and quick scene ideas, with synchronized picture and sound. It makes a 1 to 16 second clip at 540p, 720p, or 1080p, including vertical 9:16 and 3:4 frames.
Vidu's faster image-to-video model for social clips, animatics, and quick iterations from one still, with synchronized picture and sound. It makes a 1 to 16 second clip at 540p, 720p, or 1080p.
Vidu's fast first-and-last-frame model for morphs, before-and-after shots, and storyboard fills. It bridges a start image and an end image in a 1 to 16 second clip at 540p, 720p, or 1080p.
Vidu's fast reference-to-video model for character clips and social drafts that should keep a subject recognizable. It uses 1 to 7 reference images in a 3 to 16 second clip at 540p, 720p, or 1080p.

Vidu's reference-to-video model for character-driven scenes that follow a prompt while keeping the person recognizable. It uses 1 to 7 reference images in a 3 to 16 second clip at 540p, 720p, or 1080p.

Vidu's balanced reference-to-video model for a specific subject performing a new action, with a consistent look and synchronized sound. It uses 1 to 7 reference images in a 1 to 16 second clip at 720p or 1080p.

Vidu's short-drama model for scripted episodes with dialogue, character placement, and film-style camera work. It plans the shots from a script and 1 to 14 reference images, in an 8 to 12 second 1080p clip at 16:9 or 9:16.

Vidu's portrait model for spokespersons, lessons, and character close-ups that need realistic expression. It animates one portrait and can match the mouth to a supplied audio track, at 540p, 720p, or 1080p.
Vidu's multi-frame model for detailed storyboards and pose sequences where each supplied image should appear in order. It animates a start frame plus up to eight more frames, at 540p, 720p, or 1080p.
Vidu's fast portrait model for talking-head clips, virtual presenters, and avatars. It animates one portrait and can match the mouth to a supplied audio track, at 540p, 720p, or 1080p.
Vidu's fast multi-frame model for storyboards and pose sequences that should pass through specific images. It animates a start frame plus up to eight more frames, at 540p, 720p, or 1080p.

Vidu's template story model for themed short films that place your characters into a ready-made plot, such as a love story, a workday, or Journey to the West. It builds the film from your character images and the chosen template.
Vidu's one-click ad model for product showcases and promotional clips with narration. It turns 1 to 7 product images into a 10 to 60 second ad in Chinese or English.
Vidu's one-click film model for montages, travel pieces, and photo albums turned into a finished cut. It assembles 1 to 7 images into a 10 to 180 second film.
Vidu's trend-replication model for social clips that follow a reference video's pacing, cuts, and style. It rebuilds that look with 1 to 7 of your own images, at 540p, 720p, or 1080p.

xAI's precise text-to-image model for design, photography, and illustration that need close prompt following, planned typography, and sharp small text. It generates up to 10 images at 1K or 2K, including wide 21:9 and 5:2 frames, with a low or medium quality setting.

xAI's image editor for restyles, combined references, and iterative changes that follow the prompt while keeping the source recognizable. It edits one to three source images at 1K or 2K, with a low or medium quality setting.
xAI's text-to-image model for high-volume prototypes, creative variants, and everyday visuals. It generates images at 1K or 2K across square, portrait, landscape, and ultrawide frames.

xAI's video extension model for continuing a clip from its last frame with new prompt-guided action. It appends 2 to 10 seconds and keeps the source shape, up to 720p.

xAI's text-to-speech model for voiceovers, narration, and phone audio, with expressive delivery and inline speech tags such as pauses and whispers. It speaks multiple languages, including Chinese, Japanese, and Spanish, through built-in voices or a custom voice.

xAI's speech-to-text model for meeting notes, call recordings, and captions from a public audio URL. It returns word-level timestamps, and can label speakers, transcribe channels separately, and bias the transcript toward names and product terms.
